label: Farm support, from the state budget
detail: The búvörusamningar plus other support, nominal 2024. Extended by a year to end-2027 on 4 June 2026.
source: Agricultural University of Iceland, Rit LbhÍ nr. 169

label: Farm support, paid by consumers at the border
detail: Market price support: delivered through tariffs and quotas, not through the Treasury. 2020 figure, and it sits on top of the budget line rather than inside it.

label: Regional development
detail: Byggðastofnun's operating appropriation is 212 m ISK for 2026; the visible byggðaáætlun grant lines run to a few hundred million more.

label: Fishing fee collected from the industry
detail: The veiðigjald is a charge on the industry, not a subsidy to it: 19.5 bn assessed, 17.3 bn collected for the 2026 fee year.

label: Farm support from the state budget
detail: What the Treasury actually pays farmers today.

label: Gross contribution to the EU budget
detail: Not a forecast. The observed 2026 range for high-income members — Denmark 0.87%, Germany 0.88%, Luxembourg 0.94%, Finland and the Netherlands 0.96%, Ireland 1.00% of GNI — applied to an economy of Iceland's size. Iceland's GNI is not its GDP, so read this as an order of magnitude.
source: EU General Budget 2026, statement of revenue; Statistics Iceland

detail: Full rate reached in the tenth year

label: Farm support from the budget
detail: Partly replaced. CAP direct payments are the one large channel — but a new member enters at 25% and reaches the full rate in year ten, and the envelope is a negotiated annex figure, not a formula.

label: Farm support at the border
detail: Not replaced by any grant. The customs union dissolves it, and it reappears as lower shop prices rather than as a transfer. Iceland's food price level is 55.8% above the EU average.

label: Northern agriculture aid
detail: Continues, out of Iceland's own budget. All of Iceland is north of 62°N, and Article 142 of the 1994 Act of Accession lets Finland pay €293m a year and Sweden SEK 413m of national money. The EU permits the spending; it does not fund it.

label: Regional development
detail: Almost nothing comes back. At 128% of the EU average Iceland is a more-developed region: roughly €18 per head a year against €207 in less developed regions, and excluded outright from the Cohesion Fund. Luxembourg's entire seven-year allocation is €29.8m.

label: Fisheries
detail: No EU key exists. EMFAF allocations are frozen 2014–2020 shares and a new member has none, so one would have to be invented in the negotiation. The fund is small and cannot finance vessels or capacity.

label: EEA Grants donor obligation
detail: Ends outright — a true offset. Iceland is currently a donor to the €1.805bn EEA Financial Mechanism, not a recipient. Its own share is not published anywhere reachable; the widely repeated 3% is unconfirmed.

label: Contribution to the EU budget
detail: Starts, in full, from year one — while receipts phase in over a decade. This is the largest single line in the whole picture and it is the one the offset question usually leaves out.
